statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Nasdaq-100 venues are closed for the weekend after an orderly, contained Friday session; the macro backdrop remains difficult but no pathological price path is possible while trading is halted.
recommendation: Tail sits well below the block threshold across the published window because CME equity-index futures and the NAS100 CFD are shut until Sunday 22:00Z. Stress stays elevated as a description of the bond, energy and inflation-expectation backdrop rather than of any in-window exposure.
headline: Weekend closure follows an orderly Nasdaq-100 finish; Tail at the floor, Stress elevated on yields and energy
body: The Nasdaq-100 closed Friday at 30,608.14, up 0.42%, inside a contained 30,413.59-30,667.56 range and roughly 60 points below the session high, so the observed path showed no persistent one-way structure, no shallow-pullback signature and no session-extreme holding. VIX eased 5.1% to 14.87, finishing at the day's low, and WTI settled near $92.4, down 2.3% on the day and about 7.4% on the week after reports of US-Iran talks on a phased deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. That relief sits against a genuinely stressed backdrop: the 10-year yield printed as high as 5.23% this week, an area last seen in 2007, the 30-year reached its highest level since 2004, market-implied odds of an October Fed hike are around 71%, final September University of Michigan sentiment fell to 48.1 with year-ahead inflation expectations at 4.6%, and WTI is still up roughly 12% on the month with the Hormuz blockade unresolved. CME equity-index futures settled for the week at 21:00Z and do not reopen until Sunday 22:00Z, which is beyond the final published forecast slot. Every hour in this assessment therefore falls inside a scheduled market closure, so Tail is held near its floor: mean-reversion failure requires a tradable price path, and none exists. Stress is retained in the elevated band because the yield and energy regime is unresolved and will be tested next week by August PCE on Wednesday, ISM Manufacturing on Thursday and the September employment report on Friday. The principal conditional risk is gap formation at the Sunday reopen should weekend Hormuz diplomacy advance or collapse; that would be scored on the observed path once trading resumes, not anticipated here.

lookbackSummary: Over the trailing 24 hours the published Claude state stayed between Tail 17 and 22, alternating green and yellow without ever reaching the block threshold. European and early US hours carried the firmest readings, with three trend-up prints between 06:00Z and 11:00Z as the index worked higher, before the afternoon settled back into mixed conditions and Tail drifted to 18-19 into the cash close. The 13:00Z hour has no published assessment and is marked unavailable. Stress held in a narrow 54-59 band throughout, reflecting a persistent yield and energy backdrop rather than any single event.
outlookSummary: The entire published forecast window falls inside the scheduled CME weekend closure: futures settled at 21:00Z on Friday and do not reopen until Sunday 22:00Z, past the final slot. Tail is therefore held between 9 and 12 across all 24 hours, since mean-reversion failure requires a tradable price path. Stress eases from 50 toward 45 through the quiet overnight and Saturday hours and firms back to 50 into the end of the window as unpriced weekend headline flow accumulates ahead of the reopen. Confidence decays gently from 88 to 82 purely as the last verified Friday observation ages. The mapped policy state stays EA_ON for every published slot. The main conditional risk, gap formation at the Sunday reopen driven by Hormuz diplomacy or a renewed yield impulse, sits outside this window and will be scored on the observed path once trading resumes.
